RAISIN CONCENTRAGTE
TERMINOLOGY:

Raisin concentrate is the name given to the pure concen~
trated extract of raisins prepared by leaching the raisins with
water. The leaching process is undertaken in several stages to
procuce raisin juice, The liquid is then processed in a vacnum
pan, where the excess water is evaporated to obtain a desired 70¢
brix concentration or 70¢ natural fruit soluble solids.

SOURCES:

The major area of production of raisins is California but
Australia and certain areas of the Middle Fast are also producers,
Fatty acid esters have been used for many years in Australia and
the Middle East to reduce the drying time of the grapes (1).

Thie shorter drying time is caused by the interaction of esters
in the dip with the waxy surface of the grapes to increase the
rate of water loss during drying. In contrast, most California
raisins are sun dried without the use of a drying aid, which
results in a raisin with a blue-black color, darker than that of
Australian raisins,

Raisin concentrate ig manufactured from two different types
of raisins, Thompson seedless and Muscats. Each type of concen-
trate has its own distinctive flavor differing chemically in pH
due to the amount of tartaric acid present (2). The range of
tartaric acid in the Thompson seedless concentrate is 1,3-2.0%
giving it a pil} range of 3.0-3.5. The Muscat concentrate has a
concentration range of 0.7~0.9% tartaric acid with a PH of
4.0-4.5,

USAGE:

Raisin concentrate is used in the commercial bakery produc-
tion of breads as an anti~staling agent, a natural coloring
agent, and as a substitute for sucrose, refiners syrup, and
molasses in flavoring and sweetening, The two major sugars found
in raisin concentrate are fructose ana glucose, found in nearly
egual amounts (3). Because raisin concentrate has no sucrose
content and is a source of natural brown color, it also has
applications in the manufacture of natural and healthfooa goods.
Raisin concentrate is also used as a flavor and humidifying agent
for aromatic tobaccoe. It can be found in chew: ny tobaccos at a
level of approximately 3% and in cigarettes at 0.25-1.00% of the
casing solutions. °

Performance of Barclay Cigarettes
with Filter Grooves Blocked

An experiment has been performed co determine the variation
in ventilation level and smoke delivery of the Barclay cigarette
as 2 function of the number of filter grocves blocked. The
Barclay filter relies exclusively em peripheral air channel
grooves to provide a high level of ventilation It has been
shown thzt the lips of the smoker interact with the Filter grooves
and thus diminish the ventilacion level and increase the “tar”
delivered. The present experiment was designed to show the extent
of ventiletion decrease and "tar" increase as a function of filter
groove blockage.

Barclay cigarettes (85 mm. soft pack) were prepared by block- ~.--
ing 0, 1, 2, 3 ox 4 of the filter groove openings with tipping
glue. The glue was carefully applied such that a minimal amount
of tow wes contacted. After blocking the filter grooves, samples
of the prepared cigarettes were submitted to the R&D Analytical
Services Division for routine smoke analyses under standard FTC
smoking conditions. Pressure drep and air dilution measurements
were also performed, The results of these analyses are summarized
in Table i.

As the results summarized in Table I show, smoke component
Geliveries increased dramatically with the number of filter grooves
blocked, The FIC "tar" delivery increased from 1.8 mg/cigt. with
no grooves blocked co 11.7 mg./ cigt. with all four grooves glued
shut. Other measured smoke component deliveries as well as clpa-
rette drafts (DHO) increased as well. Air dilucion levels
decreased from 67.0% with no grooves blocked to 11,9% with four
grooves blocked (Table I). FTC “tar,” carbon monoxide (CO),
cigarette draft (DHO) and air dilution were found to vary exponen-
tially with the number of filter grooves blocked (figures 1, 2, 3,

4, respectively). Linear regression coefficients for these models
are summerized in Table II.

The results of the experiment show that as the Barclay filter
groaves are closed off, the level of ventilation decreases sub-
stantially. As a consequence, FTC "tar" and other smoke component
(i.g. nicotine, CO, etc.) deliveries increase exponentially The
mathematical models for the relationships between groove blockage .
and analytical measurements can be used to estimate the number of W

DEVELOPMENT PROJECT SUMMARY FOR THE MONTH OF JANUARY, 1973
TITLE: Expanded Tobacco
OBJECTIVE:
Improved filling capacity.
DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES:
Complete Tobacco Blend "Stiffening" - Jetstream and ADT Dryers
Comparison runs with the closed loop ADT dryer and the
Jetstream unit showed a compacimeter filling power increase in
the range of 12-9% respectively when compared to regular ADT
dryer. Initial flavor group evaluation of finished cigarets
at both equal weight and a ?% weight reduction, show differences
primarily attributable to differences in cigaret delivery versus
the new drying operation. Cigarets designed to give equal
delivery versus control will be necessary to see if any real
subjective differences occur due to the processing step.
ADT Dryer Optinization
The experimental pilot plant ADT dryer setup is designed
to also examine air drying parameters as well as those of the
closed loop operation, First runs have begun with 2 goal of
determining relative drying contribution of this convective-
conductive type dryer.
Water Impregnation - Expansion
First attempts at moving the impregnation step from bench
scale equipment to small pilot scale units resulted in a
decrease of a significant portion of the expansion previously
seen (50 vs. 75 cc/l10 gms.). Subsequent studies show short
vacuum release time and minimum "clumping" of fibers are
required to obtain a high degree of expansion. Present
material from this study is in the 60-65 cc/1l0 gms. range
erimarily due to accelerated vacuum release.

FINAL REPORT TO CIAR
~ Tables of sample sizes for determining the significance of mutation frequencies
(1) have proved useful to geneticists who face the problem of testing the
. significance of observed increases in mutation frequencies. These tables were
derived on the assumption that the observed number of mutations is a Poisson
variable. More often than not, however, the reported number of mutations is, in
- fact, the sum of mutations observed in several reptications of the same
experiment. Such replication introduces additional variation (overdispersion),
that is not accounted fos if only the aggregate is considered in the analysis. This
7 failure to account for such overdispersion affects the statistical analyses employed
to determine the significance levels of differences between groups or
experimental treatments. In particular, such deviations from the Poisson, together
with the use of Poisson-based statistical tests can lead to an excess of “false
positive” results, The ultimate objective of our CIAR-sponsared research is to
- provide a correction for the overdispersion in Poisson-based statistical tests,
thereby reducing the Type I error rates.
- In pursuing this objective, we sought to characterize data sets by mathematical
models that are more realistic than those generally encountered in the research n
_ literature, That is to say, we eschewed the simplistic assumptions of Poisson and oO
binomial distributions in favor of “models” that might better characterize the .O]
observed data. Some of these “models” - the negative-binomial and the beta- ©
= binomial - are well-known to statisticians, and are often used by them. Yet, only i
rarely, if ever, are they to be found in the literature of practidoner-biologist (A)
Others, such as the Pearson-type distributions, have been in the statistics literature 3

In the present 21-day inhalation study the influence of SIDESTREAM
and MAINSTREAM CIGARETTE SMOKE of the standard reference cigarette
type 2@Rt on selected responses of free lung cells (FLC) will be
investigated.
The objectives of this study are:
(1) the application of flow cytometry in combination with or
in place of conventional FLC methods and
(2) the selection of a reproducible lavage method for future
studies.
144 rats will be randomly allocated to 3 groups, 60 for sham
control, 60 for mainstream smoke and 24 for sidestream smoke
exposure. The head-only exposure will be performed for 420
minutes/day at 0.27 milligrams/liter total particulate matter
— (TPM) corresponding to a daily dose of 120 minutes x milligram,
liter TPM for mainstream smoke and at 0.07 milligrams/liter TEM
corresponding to a daily dose of 35 minutes x milligram/liter TPM
for sidestream smoke. Rats will be exposed 7 days/week for a
period of 21 days. Thais study will be divided into 3 subsequent
: experiments. Sidestream exposure will only take place in the 3rd
2 experiment.

2 cally. The microbiological quality controls will include the

TOBACCO SMOKE-INDUCED ALTERATIONS OF CYTOKERATIN EXPRESSION IN THE RAT NASAL

CANTTY FOLLOWING CHRONIC INHALATION OF ROOM-AGED SiDESTREAM SMOKE

Sentage, W.K., Balles, H', Friedrichs, D.", Kuhn, M.), Teradesai, A.', Terpstra, P27,

‘INBIFO Intitut fur biclogischa Forschung Gmbh, Fuggers. 3, Kéin, Germany;

« °ORC Contact Research Center, Zaventem, Belglum Supported by Philip Morris USA

Envirommental tcbacee smoke (ETS) is a highly diluted mixture of sidestream smoke

and exhaled mainstream smoke. It undergoes chemical and physical changes in

composition due to aging, @.g., by coniact with various surfaces over time [1]. Ina

chronic (12 month) inhalation study on rets using room-aged sidesiream smoke

(RASS) as an experimantat surrogate for ETS, we investigated differentiation

changes, ie., altered cytokeratin (CK) expression, In the epithelial lining of the res-

piratory tract, and the correlation of such charges with classical histopatholagical

findings. The dose was 12 Lg TPM / | for 6h / d (upper limits of typical ETS

concentrations are up to 100-fold lower). Wa recenily developed an immunohisto-

chemical methed to investigate complex Ci expression patterns in routine parafiin

sections from rat respiratory tract tissues using a panel cf moncclonal antibodies

with defined specificity for rat CK [2]. Using this technique, we could detect CK

expression changes at various sites of the rat respiratory tract that oceurred after 3

days of expcsure to the same daily dose of RASS (3]

The histopathological findings seen after 12 months of exposure were similar in

quatity and severity to those seen ajtor 8 days of exposure, 1¢., reserve-call hyper-

plasia and squamous metaplasia of the nonciliated respiratory epithelium of maxtito-

turbinate, tateral wall, and nasoturbinate at nasal cavity lavel 1(NL1} (levels acc. to

[4]. No findings were observed at level 2 (NL2). Changas in CK expression were ob-

served at the sites where histcpathalogical findings were scen, ¢.9.. enhanced ex-

pression of CK14 in basal and nonteiliated cells at NL1. Additionally, CK expression

changes were seen at siies of NL1 and NL2 where thore were no histopathological

findings, ¢.g., enhanced expression of CK14 in basal cells of the respiratory epithe-

fiurn and in submucosal glands and gland ducts at the septal region of NL2. In cur

presentation, detailed results obtained for 8 different CK antibodies following 12

months of exposure will be given and compared to the results obtained for 8 days of

exposure.

Summary

Nitrosation of naturally occurring tobacco alkaloids is commonly accepted as the

mechanism of tobacco specific nittosamine (TSNA) fermation in tobacco. As

minimal-to-no TSNA are present in green tobacco, TSNA formation and

accumulation are generally consideyed to occur during curing. Most recent

hypotheses focus an microbial reduction of nitrate to nitrite and other oxides of

curing. This natural microbial process remains the prevalent hypothesis for

formation of TSNA, indepencent of microbial activity, is presented in this work on

flue-cured tobacco.

it is common practice to flue-cure Virginia or blonde tobacco in bulk bams tnat

incorporate forced air ventilation and temperature control. Modern bulk barns

generally use liquid preeane gas (LPG) with direct-fired burners thai exhaust

combustion gases directly into the barn where the tcbacco is exposed to those

combustion gases. Our studies indicate tat LPG combustion by-products,

namely NO,, (in the exhaust stream ot direct-fired, tlue-cured barns) react with

naturally occurring tobacco alkaloids to forrn TSNA. Heat exchange curing

methods preclude exposure of the curing tobaccs to combustion gases and by-

products, thereby eliminating this signiicant source of TSNA tarmation, without

degrading leaf quality or smoking character. Research findings fram 1998 and

1939 will be presented to demonstrate the significance of direct-firad curing as a

source of TSNA formation in flue-cured tobacco.

INTRODUCTION N
: ~°
Environmental tobacco smoke {ETS) {s present in the indoor air of places where if
people smoke. Considerable attention is currently focused on ETS because of §
reports (1, 2) concluding that long term exposure to ETS is associated with ‘
disease. However, these conclusions come from epidemiological studies lacking t
validated measures of ETS exposure. In response to this deficiency, researchers Ts
throughout the world are analyzing indoor air to assess ETS exposure in field ‘
settings. Currently, efforts are hampered by the lack of an ideal indicator (2) Y
of ETS. Nicotine and respirable suspended particles (RSP) have found the t
greatest use as surrogate indicators of ETS exposure; nevertheless, until fairly
recently, few investigations involved measurements of both indicators. Against (
this background, some have attempted to evaluate or predict concentrations of j
nicotine or RSP by assuming that defined ratios of the two substances exist.
Using nicotine and RSP data from field surveys, we show here that the
relationship between the two is too weak for purposes of either evaluation or
prediction.
MATERIALS AND METHODS
Data are from surveys performed in three public, environmental categories:
offices (3, 4), restaurants (3, 5), and passenger cabins of commercial aircraft
(6}. For the surveys, RSP and nicotine samples were collected concurrently with
portable air sampling systems (4). Sampling and analytical procedures have been on
described previously (7, 8). Statistical interpretation proceeded from data Zz
for each of the three individual environmental categories. Correlations were &
evaluated between raw and Jog transformed RSP and nicotine concentration values; ny
Pearson’s correlation coefficients were computed. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test 7
(9) was used to assess whether RSP to nicotine ratios were better approximated

weenie a * The Fontham study is the largest case-control study of
: . lifetime nonsmokers and lung cancer reported to date in the
scientific literature, involving 431 nonsmoking cases and
794 population controls.

* The authors state that the study vas designed specifically
to address coma of the methodological faults of previous
studies of ETS and lung cancer, including inadequate
attention to confounding factors and misclassification of
smoking status and inadequate confirmation of lung cancer
diagnosis.

* The authers claim that the study provides the strongest
available evidence that ETS increases the risk for lung
cancer in nonsmokers.

MATOR. FINCINGS

* The study reports a statistically significant relative risk
for adenocarcinoma of 1.47 based on spousal smoke exposure.

* The study reports a statistically significant dose-response
trend for adenocarcinoma based on spousal smoking, noting
increased risk with increased expogure

* ETS exposure in the workplace and social settings also is
addressed, The authors report a statistically significant
40 to 60 percent increase in adenocarcinoma risk with ETS
exposure in both settings.

* No significant association is reported between exposure to
ETS in’ childhood and risk of lung cancer.
